page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8488C processor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs, consisting of 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base speed of 3.2 GHz. The processor cache configuration includes 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 105 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong performance in single-threaded and multi-threaded operations. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2074.0 and a multi-core score of 15951.0, both falling into the top 25% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 33.6 GB/sec, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 13.85 GB/sec, also ranking in the top 25%. In contrast, multi-core stress-ng CPU performance at 35034.78 and Passmark CPU score at 48904.2 sit in the middle 50% average tier. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 2625.73 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 162.39 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

The c7i-flex.8xlarge is designed for compute-intensive workloads that benefit from advanced instruction sets, such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for deep learning and cryptography. It demonstrates strong capabilities in static web serving at 51.12 GB/sec and text processing. For small-scale language model inference, it achieves 286.26 tokens/sec for text generation on a 135M model, though performance drops to 18.95 tokens/sec for a 7B model. The flex instance family offers a cost-efficient alternative within the compute-optimized class by delivering high resource density and strong single-core performance without the premium cost of fixed-performance instances, making it suitable for batch processing, web serving, and moderate database operations.
